selected_decision.what_happened: ERCOT, responding to Governor Abbott's August 3rd, 2026 directive for a comprehensive verification and audit of data centers in the interconnection process, paused the Batch Zero study process, asked the Public Utility Commission to excuse the August 7th, 2026 classification deadline and allow conditional classification by August 31, 2026 so eligibility could be verified first, and set a December 10th, 2026 target for filing the Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report. Seely said verification would come before the interconnection study begins and that the April 9, 2027 study deadline would be missed.
selected_decision.owner_evidence: Chad Seely, ERCOT senior vice president of regulatory policy and general counsel, is the named ERCOT executive who set out the verification-first sequence, the request for information timing, and the December 10th filing goal in public statements reported on August 14th and August 21st, 2026. The ERCOT August 20th, 2026 presentation is the operational record of the plan; it does not name Seely, so his ownership rests on the independent reporting of his statements.
selected_decision.alternative_available: ERCOT could have kept the August 7th, 2026 classification deadline in Planning Guide section 9.3.1(2)(a) and classified large loads before the eligibility verification was complete, instead of asking the Commission to delay classification to August 31, 2026.
selected_decision.ai_nexus: Batch Zero is ERCOT's study of large loads, mostly data centers and AI computing campuses, requesting grid connection in Texas. The verification gate decides which of those loads keep their place in the interconnection study. Under the Batch Zero rules, ERCOT sorts each large load into base load, studied load, or a load that does not qualify, and the verification gate governs that sorting.
selected_decision.texas_consequence: The audit covers about 250 to 300 projects, most of them data centers, representing about 200 gigawatts of future demand. Large loads that do not pass verification or do not respond are disqualified from Batch Zero. Developers seeking grid connection and the utilities that serve them face the timeline, and the study deadline of April 9, 2027 will be missed by ERCOT's own account.
selected_decision.next_check: ERCOT's Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report, which ERCOT plans to file with the Public Utility Commission by December 10, 2026, and the new Batch Zero study timeline that ERCOT says it has not yet set.

evidence_for: ERCOT's August 20th, 2026 presentation sets out a dated verification process with a December 10th, 2026 filing.
Seely's statements, reported by two independent outlets, match the sequence in ERCOT's record.
ERCOT's presentation states that the verification gate precedes final classification, giving the process a stated reason.
evidence_against: Seely said ERCOT is still working on a new Batch Zero timeline, so the schedule beyond December is not set.
The ERCOT presentation does not name Seely, so individual ownership rests on the reporting of his statements.
The governor's directive, the PUCT rule, and ERCOT's filings are separate decisions, and this profile covers only ERCOT's sequencing choice.
analysis.structural_read: The decision moves the grid's largest pending load requests through an audit before the interconnection study, and it converts a classification deadline into a conditional classification with a later verification report. The public record shows the sequence and the dates. It does not show how many projects will pass.
analysis.forward_implication: Whether the verification report lands by December 10th, 2026, and whether it discloses the criteria used to disqualify projects, will show whether the process is measurable in time for the study that ERCOT says it will not finish by April 9th, 2027.
